findings.title: In-session conductors inherit settings.local.json, which pre-approves git push, git:*, python:* with an empty deny list
findings.lens: fences — permissions and structural enforcement vs. stated intent
findings.fix: Either (a) drop Bash from the read-only conductors and give them a read-only Bash-holding scout to dispatch, or (b) add a PreToolUse hook with matcher Bash that denies write-shaped commands (python -c/hython -c with open(...,'w'), sed -i, tee, > redirection, git push) unless an explicit env opt-in is set — the same capability-hook pattern harness/githooks/pre-push already uses. Also prune settings.local.json: 'Bash(git:*)' and 'Bash(python:*)' are blanket grants that make every agent-side fence moot.

findings.title: Backup-Branches pushes every worktree feature branch to a PUBLIC origin with no content gate; idle-loop pushes are fully silent
findings.lens: fences — permissions and structural enforcement vs. stated intent
findings.fix: Gate the push on content, not name: before each push run a cheap scan over `git diff --name-only @{u}..HEAD` (or origin/master..HEAD for new branches) against a deny-pattern list (.env*, *.pem, *.key, settings.local.json, *.log) and a secret grep, refuse + Notify on hit. Add a branch-prefix allowlist (e.g. bp*/, cto/, feat/) or an explicit -Backup switch. Remove the Out-Null at :924 so idle pushes are logged. Consider extending pre-push to refuse any push containing those paths regardless of ref.

findings.title: The conductor→writer hop (Agent tool) is governed by prose only; no dispatch allow-list exists anywhere
findings.lens: fences — permissions and structural enforcement vs. stated intent
findings.fix: Make the hop checkable: a PreToolUse hook with matcher Agent that reads subagent_type from tool_input and compares against a per-conductor allow-list JSON (conductor → permitted subagent_types); deny with reason otherwise. For gated forges, have the hook require the verdict to come from a file the gatewarden wrote (harness/state/verdicts/<slug>.json) rather than from prompt text.

findings.title: Headless profiles' denies are form-matched; Bash(hython:*) in the allow list is an interpreter that writes anything
findings.lens: fences — permissions and structural enforcement vs. stated intent
findings.fix: Apply the pre-push lesson to the other fences: a PreToolUse Bash hook that denies `hython -c`/`python -c` and shell redirection into VERSION, harness/state/**, harness/verify/*_baseline.json; and/or a versioned pre-commit hook under harness/githooks that refuses commits touching those paths without SYNAPSE_GATE_C=1. Capability, not form.

findings.title: No test pins any fence: agent tools: lines, the PreToolUse guard, Backup-Branches, or the profile deny lists
findings.lens: fences — permissions and structural enforcement vs. stated intent
findings.fix: One test module: parse every .claude/agents/*.md frontmatter; assert any description containing 'read-only'/'never edits' has tools ∩ {Write, Edit, NotebookEdit} = ∅; assert agent-settings.json and relay-settings.json deny lists still contain push/merge/VERSION/state; feed guard-edit-targets.py a VERSION path via stdin and assert deny (red today — that is the ratchet working); grep orchestrate.ps1 Backup-Branches for the master/main skip. Also note agent-settings.json allows Edit(.claude/**), which includes the agent definitions themselves.

findings.title: Board conductors never take lock.py — no mutual exclusion on loop/memory/reach STATE.json
findings.lens: state — workflow state and durability (harness/loop, harness/memory, harness/reach boards; lock.py; legs.json; ledgers)
findings.fix: Make the conductors' preflight run `python harness/lock.py acquire <board-id> --worktree <path>` and have the workflow refuse unless the args carry the lock token (exit 3 = already held). Add 'loop', 'memory', 'reach' as leg ids so status.py/statusline.py show them as running.

findings.title: Spawn cap is enforced only against the integer the conductor types in; the write-back is prose through Bash
findings.lens: state — workflow state and durability (harness/loop, harness/memory, harness/reach boards; lock.py; legs.json; ledgers)
findings.fix: Give the workflow the board path and let it read `spawned` itself (or a tiny `harness/board_state.py read loop spawned` the conductor must pipe through); have the conductor's write-back go through the same helper so the ledger append and the counter increment are one atomic operation. Pin with a test that Σ ledger.spent == spawned.

findings.title: 7 of 12 boards — including harness/reach/ with its bus receipts — are untracked: off git, off the auto-push backup
findings.lens: state — workflow state and durability (harness/loop, harness/memory, harness/reach boards; lock.py; legs.json; ledgers)
findings.fix: Commit the boards (STATE.json, bus/, notes/) and add a test or pre-commit check that every harness/*/STATE.json is tracked. Decide explicitly which dated run dirs are evidence (tracked) vs scratch (.gitignore).

findings.title: Rung readiness is hardcoded in the workflow script; STATE.json is not the gate it claims to be
findings.lens: state — workflow state and durability (harness/loop, harness/memory, harness/reach boards; lock.py; legs.json; ledgers)
findings.fix: Have the conductor pass the rung's `status` and `substrate_presence` slice from STATE.json in args (like spawnedSoFar) and let the script gate on that; or drop the hardcoded refusals and keep gating in one place. A conformance test that every rung in STATE.rungs has a matching BUDGET key and vice versa would catch drift.

findings.title: No in-progress marker on a rung; crash-resume re-dispatches the whole phase and the log append is manual
findings.lens: state — workflow state and durability (harness/loop, harness/memory, harness/reach boards; lock.py; legs.json; ledgers)
findings.fix: Write a `dispatched` record (workflow id, rung, agents, timestamp) to the board BEFORE spawning and have resume read bus/ receipts to skip agents that already have one; key ledger entries by workflow id and refuse a duplicate key on append. Give status a small enum (ready|blocked|running|closed) alongside the prose.

findings.title: The human gate is one boolean the gated agent types itself
findings.lens: gates
findings.fix: Make the arm an artifact Joe produces, not an arg the agent relays: e.g. the workflow reads harness/<board>/ARM.json (or an AskUserQuestion inside the script) carrying a Joe-typed nonce + timestamp within N minutes and the rung name, and stamps that nonce into the envelope and receipt. Same for spawnedSoFar: have the script read STATE.json itself.

findings.title: 'Read-only by design' conductors hold Bash, and no fence sees Bash writes
findings.lens: gates
findings.fix: Either drop Bash from the three conductors (they need Read/Grep/Glob/Agent for orientation) or add a PreToolUse hook on `Bash` that denies commands touching harness/state/**, VERSION, flywheel_queue.json, resolved.json, and `git merge|push|tag`. Add a test that every agent whose description says 'read-only' has no Bash/Write/Edit in its tools line.

findings.title: Decisions board: who="human" is a hardcoded literal, and the aging clock has no caller
findings.lens: gates
findings.fix: Add `--by` (required, or derived from `git config user.name` + a SYNAPSE_ACTOR env the harness sets for agents) and refuse `by=agent` for kinds that need a human. Run `decisions.py --count` with ages in the SessionStart hook or orchestrate.ps1 preflight so exit 6 actually surfaces; commit DECISIONS.md on --write or stop claiming it is the board.

findings.title: flow-conductor can bank its own authority via CronCreate
findings.lens: gates
findings.fix: Remove CronCreate from the conductor and make standings a human-run or orchestrate.ps1-owned script; if the cron must exist, have the cron job invoke a read-only agent (tools: Read, Grep, Glob only) rather than the conductor.

findings.title: 2,413 untracked files under harness/ - eight whole boards (STATE.json included) and ten battleplan ledgers exist only in the working tree
findings.lens: observability
findings.fix: Decide per-dir: commit (boards, STATE.json, ledgers, agent/workflow definitions, rulings) or .gitignore explicitly (bus/, artifacts/ scratch). A tiny check in status.py or the proposed morning script: count untracked files under harness/ and .claude/agents|workflows and print it as a line, so the number is visible even before the decision is made. The CTO_RULINGS_BP3.md + ledger files are one git add away.

findings.title: harness/status.py renders a manifest frozen on 2026-08-13 - the R140 failure class recurring one layer up
findings.lens: observability
findings.fix: Either make status.py discover boards (glob harness/*/STATE.json and print one line per board: name, status, mtime, open gates) instead of reading a single manifest, or make it fail loud when legs.json is older than the newest STATE.json / receipt (print 'MANIFEST STALE: legs.json 2026-08-13 < receipts/BP4-TIDY.json 2026-09-03' and exit nonzero). The second is a 10-line change and honours R140.

findings.title: Token/cost is recorded only for -Budget battleplan runs; the 18 workflow scripts and every conductor leave no spend record

Add a derived cost_usd from the model id table so the ledger has one number a human reads. Confirm whether status:'open' on the 09-03 ledger is a settle that never ran (orchestrate.ps1:170 says an unrecordable settle 'must be' loud).

findings.title: No tool-call budget exists in any of the 18 workflows; 'budget' means spawn count only
findings.lens: context
findings.fix: Add one line to each GROUND/brief: 'CALL BUDGET: <= N tool calls; state count used in your final line.' Start with the three GROUND-carrying workflows (loop, reach, memory-loop), then the others. Pair it with CTX-3 so the number is checked, not just asked for.

findings.title: Read-only agents are fenced only by omitting Edit/Write; Bash is an open write channel with no hook, deny, or settings fence for Agent-tool subagents
findings.lens: roster
findings.fix: Two tiers. (a) For agents that only need git log/pytest, keep Bash but add a PreToolUse matcher on Bash that denies write-shaped commands (redirection, sed -i, tee, git commit/push/merge) when the hook payload identifies a subagent - verify first whether the payload carries agent identity. (b) Correct moneta-cartographer.md:11 and the other 14 prose claims to say 'holds no Edit/Write' rather than 'read-only', so the definition stops overstating its fence.

findings.title: FLOW and REACH harnesses (3 conductors, 2 workflows, 7 board files) exist only in the working tree
findings.lens: roster
findings.fix: Joe's word first (both boards say UNRATIFIED, and committing to any feature branch publishes to the public origin). Then either commit the 12 files on master or move them under harness/retired/ with a one-line note in harness/legs.json. Do not leave them in limbo.

findings.title: No test parses agent frontmatter: neither YAML validity nor tools-fence conformance is pinned

findings.title: 18 workflow scripts, zero tests, zero golden runs, zero replay

findings.title: The PreToolUse edit guard and PostToolUse python check have no tests

findings.title: No guard against the 'control pinned to the brief's figure' class — and this review's own brief carries an instance

findings.title: STATE.json has no writer: conductors hand-edit 10-22 KB JSON through Bash, not .tmp+replace
